title: Four schools
hookLine: Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya, Gelug: later years explain each, never ranked

lines: RIVERS FROM THE SAME HIGH GROUND.
cards: Some of the great rivers of Asia begin on the Tibetan plateau. Same snow, same high ground, and then they run off through different valleys, feeding different fields, each one a whole river.
Tibetan Buddhism is a little like that. Visit four of its monasteries and you may hear four styles of chanting and meet four lines of teachers going back centuries.
Today: the four schools, just their names and a first glance.

teach.b: Nyingma means the old ones. It carries the early translations from the time of Padmasambhava, and it's known for a teaching called dzogchen, the great perfection.
Kagyu means the lineage of the spoken word. It runs from Marpa the translator to his student Milarepa, the poet who lived in mountain caves, to Gampopa, whose book gave you the four thoughts.
Its best-known teaching is mahamudra, the great seal.
Sakya is named for the gray earth where its first monastery was built, and one family, the Khön, has guided it for generations. Its central teaching is called the path and its fruit.
Gelug means the virtuous ones. It grew from the scholar Tsongkhapa and his students, with a strong emphasis on monastic discipline, study and debate; the Dalai Lamas come from this school.
What they share: the same monastic code, the Mahayana heart of bodhicitta, the Vajrayana tools of mantra and visualization. They differ in lineage, in emphasis, in which texts come first.
Later, a movement called Rime, meaning without sides, urged Tibetans to learn from all of them. And alongside the four lives Bön, Tibet's own old religious tradition, with lineages of its own.
Later years will open each school properly. For now, the names, and no ranking. Looking back at the week: check the teacher.
Take in, send out. One slogan. For all of us.

how: Tibetan Buddhists usually practice within one of the four schools, Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya or Gelug, through a particular teacher and monastery, and many also receive teachings from other schools in the nonsectarian spirit of the Rime movement.

games.q: a friend asks you which of the four schools is the real Tibetan Buddhism. what's the fair answer, the way this path teaches it?
o: the one the Dalai Lama belongs to.
each is a whole stream from the same high ground.
games.why: the four share one heart and differ in lineage and emphasis; the Rime movement itself urged Tibetans to learn from all of them.

practice: Name the four slowly, one per breath, Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya, Gelug, and picture four rivers leaving the same snowfield. Then let the names go and sit with the breath, the same breath whichever valley you're in.
When the mind wanders, come back to the high, quiet ground.

wordCard.voice: Four schools. Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Gelug: four lineages of Tibetan Buddhism, sharing one heart, each a whole way.

orig.note: Tibetan rnying ma: 'the old ones', the school carrying the earliest translations.

carryVoice: Your line: four streams. One high ground, many valleys, each a whole river. See you tomorrow.
